reader.requirement: At --std 85, END-UNSTRING must end the UNSTRING statement it follows (per §1985:IV.6.4.3: the most recently preceding unterminated UNSTRING when they nest), so that the ON OVERFLOW / NOT ON OVERFLOW imperative statements stop at it, the statements after it run whatever the overflow outcome and belong to the enclosing statement (IF branch, SIZE ERROR phrase, in-line PERFORM, an outer UNSTRING's phrase), a later conditional phrase cannot attach to the terminated UNSTRING, and an END-UNSTRING with no unterminated UNSTRING is refused.

edition-consulted.switches: END-UNSTRING is reserved at all four editions (row 'continuous since 1985')
Constructs.ConditionalPhrasesAnyOrder2002: at 85 NOT ON OVERFLOW written before ON OVERFLOW is refused (COBOL0900); the scope the terminator closes is not switched
Constructs.UnstringSenderReferenceModified2002 (a reference-modified sender), unrelated to the scope terminator

reader.edition-search: grep -rn 'END-UNSTRING|END_UNSTRING|EndUnstring' over src (excluding Generated, bin, obj): the lexer token, the grammar's optional END_UNSTRING in unstringStatement, the reserved-word row, and binder comments; grep -n UNSTRING in VersionConformancePass.cs: the ref-mod sender gate and the conditional-phrase order gate. The parse of the terminator itself is edition-blind; 85 takes the latest edition's grammar arm.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (for the scope END-UNSTRING closes; only the order of the two OVERFLOW phrases inside the scope differs: 85 requires ON OVERFLOW first)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c35 and pb1183 use END-UNSTRING only as a plain terminator; not exercised: statements after END-UNSTRING running in both overflow outcomes, a nested UNSTRING inside ON OVERFLOW whose END-UNSTRING closes only the inner, the delimited-scope UNSTRING as the imperative of IF and ON SIZE ERROR, inside an in-line PERFORM, and the refusals of a stray or doubled END-UNSTRING and a phrase after it.

reader.notes: The grammar's unstringStatement ends with an optional END_UNSTRING after the shared conditionalPhrases loop, whose association predicate gives each phrase to the nearest unterminated statement; nesting, the IF/SIZE ERROR/PERFORM containers and the refusals all matched the 1985 scope rules. The only 85-specific arm on the path is the phrase-order gate, which also behaved as the 1985 format requires.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR19 and §1985:IV.6.4.3 Scope of Statements (the most-recent-unterminated-verb rule and the nearest-unterminated-statement rule for conditional phrases). Probe s6/u1.cob at --std 85, aimed at containers the reader did not try: an UNSTRING ... ON OVERFLOW ... END-UNSTRING inside a STRING's ON OVERFLOW phrase followed by the STRING's NOT ON OVERFLOW (same phrase keyword, different verb: the NOT ON OVERFLOW must go to the STRING); a delimited-scope UNSTRING in an IF's THEN followed by ELSE, and in an ELSE followed by END-IF; an UNSTRING whose pointer starts beyond the sender (overflow at once) with an IF/ELSE/END-IF inside ON OVERFLOW and a NOT ON OVERFLOW after it. Printed V1-U-OVF / V1-S-OVF-TAIL / V1-AFTER / V2-OVF / V2-THEN-TAIL / V3-NOT / V3-ELSE-TAIL / V4-PTR-OVF / V4-AFTER, exit=0: every terminator closed exactly its UNSTRING and each following statement ran in the enclosing phrase. No 1985-only form of the terminator exists; the reader's phrase-order gate (COBOL0900) covers the later edition's any-order form. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR19 (the text is in GR19); OK §1985:IV.6.4.3 (6.4.3 Scope of Statements) the text is in the clause.
